answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it votes on a task or claims a reward. The ledger caps each deposit’s influence, and peers can submit signed evidence of duplicate control; after a challenge period, proven linked identities lose their stake. This does not make Sybils impossible, but makes influence costly: an attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, whether the aliases are named falcon, cedar, or glacier.
